
```{r}
# Generate a 30-color colorblind-friendly palette
# Uses multiple strategies to ensure good discrimination

library(grDevices)
here::iam("colour_palette.rmd")

# Method 1: Using viridis-family palettes (excellent for colorblindness)
# These are perceptually uniform and colorblind-safe
cat("Method 1: Viridis family palettes\n")
cat("=====================================\n\n")

# You'll need to install viridis package first: install.packages("viridis")
library(viridis)
palette_viridis <- viridis(30)



# Display the palette
cat("Hex codes for 30-color palette:\n")
for (i in seq_along(palette_viridis)) {
  cat(sprintf("%2d: %s\n", i, palette_viridis[i]))
}



# Method 2: Using ColorBrewer palettes (extended)
cat("Method 2: ColorBrewer approach (combining multiple palettes)\n")
cat("=============================================================\n\n")

# Combine multiple colorblind-safe ColorBrewer palettes
# These are scientifically designed for colorblindness

# You can use RColorBrewer package: install.packages("RColorBrewer")
library(RColorBrewer)
# 
# # Get colorblind-safe qualitative palettes
palette_set2 <- brewer.pal(8, "Set2")
palette_dark2 <- brewer.pal(8, "Dark2")
palette_paired <- brewer.pal(12, "Paired")
# # Combine and extend
cb_palette_30 <- c(palette_set2, palette_dark2, palette_paired, 
                     colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"))(2))

# Display the palette
cat("Hex codes for 30-color palette:\n")
for (i in seq_along(cb_palette_30)) {
  cat(sprintf("%2d: %s\n", i, cb_palette_30[i]))
}


# Combine palettes into a single data frame for display
palette_df <- data.frame(
  Index = 1:30,
  Method_1 = palette_viridis,
  Method_2 = cb_palette_30
)
print(palette_df)

# Print recommendation
cat("RECOMMENDATION:\n")
cat("===============\n")
cat("For 30 colors, use the 'Curated' palette above.\n")
cat("It balances perceptual distinctiveness with colorblind safety.\n\n")
cat("Note: With 30 colors, some will be harder to distinguish.\n")
```
